newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka students protest against reforms.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka students protest against reforms.

text.p: Police on Wednesday fired teargas and used batons and water cannon to disperse hundreds of Sri Lankan university students demonstrating against proposed education reforms.
More than 1,000 students who gathered near the central railway station in Colombo's Fort business district waved banners and shouted slogans before police turned on them.
Police said they were forced to fire teargas after students obstructed traffic on the main road.
"They were told they could peacefully demonstrate near the station," said Tikiri Dissanyaka, deputy inspector general of police for Colombo.
"But they walked on to the busy main road, blocking traffic, leaving police no alternative but to use teargas and baton charge," he added.
Police said about 23 students had been treated for injuries.

"We were protesting against the education reforms which are aimed at undermining the free education system and depriving the poor from access to education," Chaminda Bandara, convenor of the Inter University Students Union, told Reuters Television.
Sri Lanka's People's Alliance government is considering changes in the school and university curriculum to reduce pressure on students and introduce the English language as a subject in schools.
